# RGAA mapping

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-mapping-doc.js from rule-map.js; do not edit by hand. -->

Which RGAA tests each rule checks, and which rules speak to each RGAA criterion. A scan names these tests on its results when asked (`engineOptions.mappings: ['rgaa']`, see [`ENGINE_OPTIONS.md`](https://github.com/SureA11y/core/blob/main/docs/ENGINE_OPTIONS.md#other-standards-mappings) in core); the notes below say how the mapping is made.

> **Review status:** drafted from the RGAA test wording, official methodology and glossary, then checked row by row against them; not yet reviewed by an RGAA auditor. Corrections go in `rule-map.js`; this page is regenerated from it.

A rule maps to a test when its failure (or, for a manual rule, the question it raises) is direct evidence about what the test's methodology checks. A rule that fails is linked only when its usual failures really fail the test; where that is uncertain, the test is left off or the rule asks. A mapped rule covers the test in part at most: a `pass` never means an RGAA test is conforme, and most tests need a human. A test marked "(exception)" is linked although RGAA relates it to other WCAG criteria than the rule; the reason follows the note. Where a rule's findings fail different tests, each finding counts toward its own (by its text size, its list, its role…), and a criterion's result names only the tests of the findings that decided it; the note says how. A test marked "(asks)" is one where the rule's failures are only questions, and one marked "(some findings)" is one only some of its findings count toward.

## RGAA 4.1.2

168 of 256 rules map to at least one test; they reach 80 of 106 criteria.

Not mapped to 5.8.1: only a failure if the auditor judges the table a layout table. Not mapped to 5.7.1: a table with no <td>, or a header with no cell under it, says nothing about the id, scope or role that 5.7.1 checks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `target-size-minimum`                      | automatic | 2.5.8               | —                                                                                       | Checks the 24x24 CSS px target size and spacing exception of WCAG 2.5.8, a WCAG 2.2 criterion RGAA 4.1.2 does not include. No RGAA test measures pointer target size.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `td-has-header`                            | automatic | 1.3.1               | —                                                                                       | In large tables (4x4 or more, no colspan/rowspan, and no role other than table, grid or treegrid) that have header cells, fails a non-empty <td> with no headers attribute and no header cell (<th>, or role columnheader or rowheader) above it in its column or before it in its row; a large table with no header cell at all is asked about once (TD_TABLE_NO_HEADERS), as it may be a layout table (F46). Not mapped to 5.7.4: that test covers cells "associée à un ou plusieurs en-têtes possédant un attribut id", and a cell with no header at all is not one. Not mapped to 5.6.1/5.6.2: a cell without associated headers does not show that the headers were not declared with <th>; rgaa-data-table-headers-review asks the 5.6 question about a table with no header cell.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `text-spacing-content-loss`                | automatic | 1.4.12              | 10.12.1                                                                                 | In a browser, applies the four spacings of 10.12.1 step 1 (line-height 1.5, 2em after paragraphs, letter-spacing 0.12em, word-spacing 0.16em) as a style sheet that wins over the page's own, and fails text that an ancestor with overflow hidden or clip then cuts off by at least half a line. That is the criterion's question, « le texte reste-t-il lisible ». It asks about text pushed out by less, text that comes to overlap other text, and a style sheet rule that forces spacing below those values with !important.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `textbox-name-present`                     | automatic | 4.1.2               | —                                                                                       | Checks that role=textbox has a name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, title or an associated label. It accepts a wrapping <label> and a placeholder on a text-like <input>, which 11.1.1 does not list, so a placeholder-only field passes here while it fails 11.1.1. Not mapped to 11.1.1: rgaa-field-label-listed-source reports 11.1.1 for every form field, from the sources 11.1.1 lists only. Not mapped to 7.1.1: it passes when an accessible alternative exists.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `tooltip-name-present`                     | automatic | 4.1.2               | —                                                                                       | Flags role=tooltip with an empty name, which in practice means an empty tooltip. A tooltip is supplementary content, not an operable component whose name 7.1.1 step 2 evaluates. None of the candidate tests checks tooltip content, so a fit to 7.1.1 would be weak.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `treeitem-name-present`                    | automatic | 4.1.2               | 7.1.1                                                                                   | Checks that role=treeitem has a non-empty name. A tree item is part of a script-driven tree component, and 7.1.1 step 2 requires an explicit name.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `valid-lang`                               | automatic | 3.1.2               | —                                                                                       | Fails lang on elements other than <html> whose primary subtag is not in the IANA language subtag registry (WCAG 3.1.2, ACT de46e4). Not linked to 8.8.1: the registry leaves out the three-letter ISO 639-2 codes of languages with a two-letter one (fra, fre, eng, ger), which the glossary "Code de langue" accepts, so this rule fails lang="fra", which 8.8.1 passes. rgaa-valid-lang reports 8.8.1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `video-caption`                            | manual    | 1.2.2               | 4.3.1, 4.4.1                                                                            | Asks about a <video> without a <track kind="captions"> (with a src), the question of 4.3.1 step 2 (are synchronised captions present?). A video with only kind="subtitles" tracks is asked about too, since the glossary "Sous-titres synchronisés" (note 2) does not count translation subtitles as captions. A video with a captions track is asked whether its captions are complete (CAPTIONS_REVIEW, F8), which is 4.4.1: are the captions relevant? By reason code: `CAPTIONS_REVIEW`: 4.4.1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `video-poster-text-alternative-present`    | automatic | 1.1.1               | —                                                                                       | Checks that a <video poster> has an accessible name. No RGAA 4.1.2 test targets poster images: the theme-1 tests list img/area/input/svg/object/embed/canvas, and the theme-4 tests are about transcripts, captions and AT compatibility of the media player, not naming a <video>.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `widget-keyboard-focusable`                | manual    | 2.1.1               | 7.3.1                                                                                   | Asks about an element with a widget role that Tab never reaches: a single widget that cannot take focus or takes it only from script (tabindex=-1), a composite widget with no tab stop, and an aria-activedescendant host that cannot take focus. A widget role means a script handles the element, so 7.3.1 condition 1 applies: the element is accessible by the keyboard. A question, as in core: a script may move focus there, and condition 2 passes the element when another keyboard-operable control does the same.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| **11.5** Dans chaque formulaire, les champs de même nature sont-ils regroupés, si nécessaire ?                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 11.5.1: `rgaa-radio-group-present`, `rgaa-same-name-checkboxes-review`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
